title: Create internal evidence pointer index for security enablement (SOC 2, pen test, subprocessors, audit log schemas)
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Goal
Create/refresh a single internal-only “evidence pointer index” so Security/GRC, Solutions Engineering, and (as appropriate) Sales can quickly locate the right artifacts and the approved sharing workflow during customer security reviews.

This is not a new evidence program and should not change contractual/approved language. It is an internal map that answers: “where is the artifact, who owns it, who can share it, under what conditions (e.g., NDA), and what’s the current/approved customer-facing summary.”

Scope (must include)
1) SOC 2 Type II evidence pointers
- Where the latest SOC 2 report + bridge letter (if applicable) are stored
- Access and sharing workflow (NDA requirements, approval steps, tracking)
- Who can approve release and typical turnaround SLA

2) Pen test / security assessment summaries
- Location of latest external pen test executive summary (customer-safe)
- Any internal-only detailed findings location (restricted)
- Guidance on what can be shared externally and when to escalate

3) Subprocessor list
- Canonical source for the current subprocessor list
- Owner and update cadence
- Customer request workflow (DPA/subprocessor questions)

4) Audit logging evidence
- Location of audit log one-pager (customer-facing)
- Location of audit log schema/event reference (internal or customer-safe depending on content)
- How to provide sample events / SIEM guidance without over-committing roadmap

Non-goals / out of scope
- Publishing evidence directly in the enablement kit (the kit should link to the process; artifacts are shared via controlled workflow)
- Creating new compliance artifacts or changing legal terms
- Building a new tool; this should be a Confluence page + minimal Drive pointers with access controls

Deliverables
- Confluence page (Restricted) titled: “Customer Security Review – Evidence Pointer Index”
- Includes a table-style index with:
  - Artifact name
  - What it is / when used
  - System of record (Confluence/Drive/other)
  - Direct link(s)
  - Owner (person/team)
  - Sharing rules (NDA? customer-only? summary-only?)
  - Last reviewed date + next review date
  - Related approved customer-facing doc (FAQ/one-pager) link

Acceptance criteria
- Page is restricted to appropriate internal groups (Security, GRC, Solutions Eng leadership, Sales leadership as approved)
- Index covers at minimum: SOC 2 report, SOC 2 bridge letter (if applicable), pen test executive summary, subprocessor list, audit log schema reference/sample events
- Links are current and do not point to personal drives
- Review completed by Security Engineering (Marcus Lin) and GRC (Olga Petrov)
- Includes a short “how to use this index” section and escalation paths

Notes / dependencies
- Should align to the customer evidence SOP and the RFP response library language (do not invent new promises)
- This index is referenced by the Security FAQ v2 and RFP response library as an internal evidence pointer

Primary reviewers
- Marcus Lin (Security Engineering)
- Olga Petrov (GRC)
- Markus Klein (Solutions Engineering) for usability
comments:
2026-01-29 (Naomi Feldman)
Creating ENG ticket for internal evidence pointer index. We keep getting ad-hoc pings for “SOC 2 link” / “pen test summary” / “subprocessors” / “audit log sample events” and the answers are inconsistent. This should centralize pointers + rules; artifacts remain controlled.

2026-02-03 (Daniel Carter)
Drafted structure for Confluence page under Security & Compliance > Compliance Evidence. Proposed sections:
- How to use this index (what it is / what it isn’t)
- Sharing rules quick reference (NDA, who can send, tracking)
- Evidence index table (SOC2, pen test, subprocessors, audit logs)
- Escalation contacts + SLAs
Requesting confirmation on allowed audience group for page restrictions.

2026-02-05 (Olga Petrov)
Approved approach. Ensure:
- SOC 2 report is never linked as “publicly accessible”; must go through NDA + tracking.
- Index should point to the SOP for evidence sharing and include the “approved email template” location.
- Add “do not forward” and “customer-specific distribution only” guidance.

2026-02-07 (Marcus Lin)
For audit logs: please separate “customer-facing one-pager” vs “internal schema reference.” Customers can receive sample event payloads upon request, but we should provide them via SE/Security with context (fields may change; no roadmap guarantees). Also include pointer to the latest UI labels/event names so field teams don’t paste stale screenshots.

2026-02-10 (Markus Klein)
Usability feedback: include a single TL;DR at top:
- ‘If prospect requests SOC 2 report → do X’
- ‘If prospect requests pen test → do Y’
- ‘If prospect requests subprocessors → do Z’
- ‘If prospect requests audit log schema/events → do W’
Also add an “Evidence we do NOT share” section to prevent accidental over-sharing.

2026-02-12 (Daniel Carter)
Implemented feedback:
- Added top-of-page workflow shortcuts + escalation path
- Added “Evidence we do NOT share by default” (internal findings, raw scan outputs, internal IR runbooks)
- Linked SOC2 workflow to the internal SOP and added reminder to log distribution
- Added audit log split: one-pager + internal schema + sample event guidance
Pending final restriction settings + final reviewers sign-off.

2026-02-18 (Olga Petrov)
Reviewed final. Confirmed links point to shared locations (not personal drives). Page access restricted appropriately. Added next review date aligned to quarterly enablement kit maintenance.

2026-02-20 (Marcus Lin)
Approved. One request: please keep the audit log schema link pointing to the canonical reference, not a screenshot or exported JSON in the page body. Otherwise good.

2026-02-20 (Daniel Carter)
Done. Updated audit log schema pointer to canonical reference only. Marking complete.
